page: Amazon Web Services c7a.16xlarge is a compute-optimized instance powered by a dedicated AMD EPYC 9R14 processor using the x86_64 architecture. It features 64 physical cores and 64 vCPUs running at 3.7 GHz, with a 1:1 physical-to-virtual core ratio. The memory configuration consists of 128 GB of high-speed DDR5 RAM operating at 5 GHz, providing 2.0 GB of memory per core. This instance does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, relying instead on network-attached storage and featuring a baseline network bandwidth of 25 Gbps.

Benchmark results indicate top-tier multi-core CPU performance, with stress-ng multi-core, Passmark CPU, and Geekbench multi-core scores all ranking in the top 10% of tested systems. The AMD EPYC processor's support for advanced instruction sets, including AVX-512 and vector neural network instructions, drives strong performance in specialized tasks. This is reflected in top-tier results for software compilation, ray tracing, and image processing. Memory performance is also robust, with cached read-only bandwidth reaching the top 10% and uncached large-block read/write speeds placing in the top 25%.

Given its high compute density and DDR5 memory speed, the c7a.16xlarge offers strong qualitative cost efficiency for compute-bound workloads that do not require local NVMe storage or GPU acceleration. It is highly capable for tasks such as software compilation, ray tracing, and medium-scale LLM inference, where its text generation speeds for 7B models rank in the top 10%. Additionally, the instance is well-suited for high-throughput web serving, database operations, and Redis deployments.
